title: Rightward erasure pass
statement: Let $w$ be a Boolean word, let $p$ be an input-head position for $w$, let $d$ be any data tape, let $\ell$ be an integer, and let $m$ be a nonnegative integer. For every $j$ with $0\le j\le m$, start the cleaner in state $1$ with data tape $d$, the marker true exactly on $[\ell,\ell+m)$, the origin marker at $0$, and all heads at $\ell$. After exactly $j$ steps, it is in state $1$ with all heads at $\ell+j$; its data and marker tapes are each blank on $[\ell,\ell+j)$ and agree with their initial contents elsewhere, while the origin marker is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $d$ is an arbitrary tape of optional Boolean symbols
$j$ is a natural number with $j\le m$
replaced:
Let $d$ be a data tape and let an interval of width $m$ start at $\ell$. For every $j
\le m$, running the interval cleaner for exactly $j$ steps from its rightward-erasure
state with all heads at $\ell$ erases the first $j$ cells of both the data and the
marker, moves all heads to $\ell + j$, and leaves the origin marker intact.
